benchmark.title: Know your limits.
benchmark.lead: A software test and a known reference block for your physical signal path.
benchmark.description: Test the selected profile with attenuation, noise, constant speed changes and a short dropout. Every pass requires valid archive CRC and file hashes. A single copy can fail the dropout test; repeated copies can recover the block.
benchmark.warning: Simulations do not certify your deck. Continuous wow/flutter, analog frequency response and clipping are not modeled. Verify a real recording before relying on a profile.
benchmark.step2: Record it on tape, then capture the recording as a WAV.
benchmark.step3: Load the captured WAV here to compare it with the known reference.
benchmark.limit: The result applies only to this reference block and selected profile. It does not certify tape capacity or reliability.
guide.title: How to store data on cassette tapes
guide.step1: Choose files, modulation and redundancy in Encode. The right-channel reference is enabled by default.
guide.step2: Generate the stereo WAV. Left carries data; right carries the 3 kHz reference. The spoken introduction is optional.
guide.step3: In Studio, connect both outputs to the deck, calibrate the level, press REC on the deck and start the countdown.
guide.step4: Rewind and capture both channels in Decode, or import a stereo WAV. Leave reference correction on and download the verified files.
guide.formatText: TVBLK003 carries 1 KiB data blocks with synchronization, CRC and 1/2/3/5 copies. TVBLK004 distributes blocks over two channels. Copies alternate channels in separate time slots. Archive CRC and file SHA-256 must pass. TVFSK001/002 and TVBLK003 remain readable.
guide.worksText: The right-channel reference tracks tape speed variations before decoding. Stereo recording and recovery are available, with CRC and SHA-256 integrity checks. Disable reference correction for legacy mono recordings.
guide.limitsText: The reference corrects timing, not missing samples or severe distortion. Higher data rates need a cleaner signal. There is no automatic splitting across tape sides. Recovery fails if no valid copy of a block remains.
guide.privacyText: Files and audio stay in this tab. No accounts or file uploads. The site integrates Google Tag Manager. Audio-device permissions are requested only when you use those controls. A compatible browser and HTTPS or localhost are needed for audio input.
guide.motionText: Operation animations follow actual progress. Audio meters use the live signal. Reduced motion disables decorative animation; hidden tabs stop visual updates.

reference.encodeNote: Enabled by default. Left carries data; right carries a continuous 3 kHz reference to correct tape speed variations. Record both channels separately. File capacity is unchanged; the WAV is twice as large.
reference.decodeNote: Enabled by default for data + reference recordings. Disable for stereo-data recordings or older mono recordings. Audio is preserved; Playback monitors L only.

ui.referenceShort: Stereo · data on the left, reference on the right
flow.hardware: Keep left and right channels separate. Match input and output sample rates in your audio settings and avoid mixing direct monitoring into playback. With a Fast Track Pro, set Mix to PB while recording.
flow.verify: Rewind the tape and capture both channels in Decode. Keep the original files until recovery is verified.
flow.troubleNote: Crackling can be caused by the sample rate configured for the audio interface, especially when input, output and the browser audio engine are not aligned. On macOS, open Audio MIDI Setup, select the interface and set input and output to 48,000 Hz (48 kHz), the sample rate TapeBytes uses for WAV files. Then disable and re-enable the input in TapeBytes to recreate the audio connection. This setting is separate from the reference tone frequency (3 kHz). If crackling persists, check levels, connections and drivers and compare a capture made with Audacity. The reference cannot restore missing audio samples.

guide.capacity: How much data can a cassette tape hold?
guide.capacityText: Capacity depends on recording time, data rate and redundancy. A C60 has 30 minutes per side: at 300 bit/s, the theoretical ceiling is 67,500 bytes before headers, metadata and pauses. At 2400 bit/s it is 540,000 bytes. Usable capacity is lower; three or five copies take more time. Encode calculates the estimate for your selected files and settings. The stereo reference improves timing recovery, not capacity.
guide.equipmentText: A stereo cassette recorder with line input and output, suitable cables, and a computer with stereo audio input and output. A USB audio interface can provide these connections. For a first software check, generate a WAV and verify it directly in Decode before recording a cassette.
guide.compatibility: Can I decode any cassette recording?
guide.compatibilityText: TapeBytes reads its own data format, including supported earlier versions. It is not a general decoder for Commodore, ZX Spectrum or Kansas City Standard tapes, nor a tool for converting music recordings into digital files. Start with a small file and verify a complete recording and recovery on your own equipment.
home.audience: For retrocomputing enthusiasts, makers and anyone interested in how digital data travels through analog sound.
decode.referenceWaiting: Enable input to measure the reference.
decode.referenceAbsent: No stable reference detected near 3 kHz.
decode.referenceMeasured: Live estimate · nominal 3000 Hz · monitoring only
studio.stopNote: Stop ends playback, including the calibration tone.
reference.modeNote: Reference enabled: data on the left, 3 kHz reference on the right. Disable it to store data on both channels. With two copies, blocks cross channels at different times; capacity is similar to one data channel.
reference.monoNote: Mono input: connect one isolated channel, never a sum of L + R. Stereo data with ×1 needs both channels; with ×2, either complete channel contains all blocks. Reference correction requires stereo. Without it, the left data channel can be read with correction disabled. Hardware validation is still required for the new stereo-data mode.
error.stereoMono: Incomplete stereo archive from a mono input. Supply both separate channels, or an isolated complete channel of a recording made with at least two copies. Do not mix L and R.
reference.dualNote: Reference off: both channels carry data. Speed tracking uses the existing in-band synchronisation; no dedicated reference is available.
audio.monoNote: Mono uses a single data channel without a reference. With stereo files, only the left channel is decoded. Connect an isolated channel, never an L+R downmix.
audio.auto: Stereo/Mono follows the channel count reported by the input when enabled. You can override it manually. Detection does not identify audio content or the presence of a reference tone.
decode.autoStopNote: After at least 0.25 s of signal above −36 dBFS, stop and decode when all captured channels remain below −42 dBFS for the selected time (1 s by default). Initial silence does not trigger it. High noise may prevent stopping; use Stop and decode.
decode.autoStopped: End of signal detected: capture stopped automatically.
